name: Typhoon Class Submarine — Origins and development
title: Typhoon Class Submarine: Origins and development
provenance: JAH Databases — public records organized in the Signature system
requirements: Shore support for maintenance and weapons handling
description: The Typhoon is the largest submarine ever built — 48,000 tonnes submerged, with a unique multi-hull design: two main pressure hulls side by side inside the outer hull, with the missile compartment between them. Developed by Sevmash (Russia (Soviet Union)), the Typhoon Class Submarine is a ballistic-missile submarine that entered service in 1981–present.
key_points: Propulsion: 2 × OK-7 pressurized-water nuclear reactors, 2 shafts
how_it_works: Ballast tanks control buoyancy for diving and surfacing; nuclear or diesel-electric propulsion drives the boat; planes and rudder steer in three dimensions underwater.

Twin pressure hulls — a design like no other submarine
Built to break through Arctic ice for missile launch
how_it_works: Ballast tanks control buoyancy for diving and surfacing; nuclear or diesel-electric propulsion drives the boat; planes and rudder steer in three dimensions underwater.
